chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Yusuf al-Tatari, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A hunted prey eaten by a group of people in Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon them is a sheep, and there is not upon the one who slaughtered it, except for a sheep.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمُونَ: People in the state of Ihram (pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a group of people in Ihram who eat hunted game?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of collective liability (jama'ah) in Ihram hunting, where the Imam establishes that a single sheep serves as the expiation for the entire group rather than individual shares. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on shared responsibility in ritual violations, distinguishing the slaughterer's role from the group's collective obligation. It provides essential context for understanding how penalties are distributed among pilgrims who hunt together during Hajj or Umrah.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Al Hakam Bin Ayman, from Yusuf Al Tatary who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A hunted prey eaten by a group of people in Ihraam’. Heasws said: ‘Upon them is a sheep, and there is not upon the one who slaughtered it, except for a sheep’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Hakam ibn Ayman from Yusuf al-Tatariy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a people who in the state of Ihram eat from the flesh of an animal which is hunted. He (the Imam) said, ‘They owe one sheep and the one who has slaughtered does not owe more than a sheep.’”
